2026-08-13 lexitrail gate_triggers [] -> [lexitrail-backend-deploy-main] (issue-77). It was the ONLY empty list in this file while carrying enforcing=true -- the pair gate.py names as its live instance of "nothing can ever be refused here". Alex authorized the deploy trigger 2026-08-13 via zz1 with five constraints, of which #5 is that lexitrail be visible to the SAME enforcement as the other projects; creating the trigger without this line satisfies that in APPEARANCE ONLY, since a green build is identical either way. The name is listed BEFORE the trigger exists, deliberately: gate.py fails open on every ambiguity, so an unknown name is inert, whereas an ungated live trigger spends. Order is bucket -> this -> trigger. NOTE the trigger is main-only DEPLOY, never a required PR status context, so it is safe to trigger-CLOSE (see the 2026-08-11 star comment in gate.py -- closing a required context is unrecoverable).

2026-08-09 `daily_build_count` IS THE FIELD YOU EDIT. Alex: "going forward it should be easy to adjust the build count as we discover what it costs per day." calibrate.py is an ADVISOR: report-only unless --write, and --write SKIPS any project with count_pinned=true while still printing what it would have advised. Without the pin an operator's tuned number would be reverted by the next calibration — the edit that looks authoritative being the one the machine silently overwrites.

_exempt_configs._why: PERMANENTLY EXEMPT FROM REFUSAL — hcl@ decision 2026-08-11, measured at origin/main. These are NOT PR test paths: no trigger fires them, `terraform apply` does, via local-exec with on_failure=fail. A quota refusal fails step 0, aborts the apply mid-run, and the image feeding the live marketing/IG crons goes stale. zz1 had recorded cloudbuild-e2e.yaml as 'the only genuinely ungated config' and as a GAP; it is three configs, they are one class, and the class is deliberately exempt.
_exempt_configs._but: THE COUNTER CANNOT SEE THEM, AND THAT IS THE REAL PROBLEM (hcl@, measured): the gate increments only on builds running quota-gate in cloudbuild.yaml, so these three never reach it. On 08-11 the Cloud Build API showed familylore at 10 builds while the counter store read 5 — e2e alone was 3. So roughly half of familylore's real spend is invisible to the number the gate enforces against, and the gated PR path is refused against a denominator that cannot see the largest consumer. Exempt from REFUSAL is not the same as exempt from COUNTING, and today they are both.

lexitrail._count_reason: EXPLICIT FLOOR, not derived. lexitrail ran 1 build in the 168h calibration window, far below the 20 samples a p90 needs, so calibrate.py correctly refused to invent a number — and left the field ABSENT while `enforcing` stayed true. hcl@ caught that on #8199: a project claiming enforcement with no count is exactly the 'fallback that is also a legitimate value' hazard this file's own comment names. 5/day is ~35x its observed rate (0.14/day) and costs $0.03/day at its measured $0.0061/build, inside its $0.05 target. Pinned so calibration does not overwrite a deliberate floor with a number derived from one sample.

_rates_comment: 2026-08-08 — RATE RAISE REVERTED, and the reason is the whole lesson. I first raised these ~2x because the ledger under-read the invoice. But I ALSO corrected cost_of_build's span from startTime..finishTime to createTime..finishTime in the same change. Those were TWO fixes for ONE symptom: the rates were derived as (SKU dollars / minutes_SHORT), so applying them to the now-longer span computes SKU_dollars x (minutes_LONG / minutes_SHORT) and double-counts. Queue time is ~30% of stopbystop's bill and ~16.5% of ensemble's, so the compounded error runs +20% to +43% HOT per project; costed over all 613 real 08-07 builds it was $30.74 against a $24.30 invoice, +26.5%. With these original rates and the corrected span it is $24.78, +2.0%. A ledger that reads 26% hot refuses builds a quarter earlier than the real budget requires — under enforcement that is a CI outage caused by an accounting error. KEEP THE SPAN FIX; the rates were never the defect.
_allowance_comment: 2026-08-08 — RAISE AND RATCHET, per Alex: 'Raise and ratchet down.' Allowances start at roughly TODAY'S MEASURED ACTUAL (24h, this repo's own cost_of_build with the corrected span: ensemble $7.99, stopbystop $4.52, market-explorations $3.84, familylore $0.06, lexitrail $0.00 = $16.42/day) so enforcement binds from today WITHOUT stopping CI, then tightens 12% per day toward the $5.00/day fleet target. THE RATCHET IS DATA, NOT A REMINDER: reconcile.py derives today's allowance from anchor_utc + step_pct + target, so it tightens whether or not anyone remembers to tighten it, and it floors at target rather than overshooting. Alex also transferred the enforcing decision: 'enforcing flag - yes and don't ask me, your decision fully going forward, until i say otherwise' — so the stopbystop _hold is lifted and every project ships enforcing=true.
_gate_comment: 2026-08-08 — WHICH TRIGGERS THE HOURLY GATE MAY CLOSE, and the exclusions are the safety property. Alex: 'build such system that opens gate every hour, allows the builds that can be done within quota and then closes it again for an hour if necessary.' The gate closes TEST triggers only. DELIBERATELY NEVER GATED, because closing them breaks shipping rather than saving money: ⚠️ REMOVED 2026-08-10 — this entry named `ensemble-build-epod-push`, A TRIGGER THAT DOES NOT EXIST. Verified from three seats (adm@, mpl@, mcl@) and again here, both regions, with a control: `grep -c epod` = 0 while `grep -c ensemble-build-orch-push` = 1, so the probe works. This is the SELF-SUPPRESSING kind of wrong — a reader who looks for it finds nothing and concludes THEY searched badly, so it never generates a report. It survived a commit whose subject was literally 'correct a never-gate exemption', because I fixed the defect I had been told about and did not re-read the sentence around it. The epod build configs are exempt on their own merits (deploy/cloudbuild-build-epod.yaml, terraform-invoked); no trigger-name exemption is needed or valid, ensemble-build-orch-push / -pr and ensemble-build-ci-base-push (orchestrator and CI base image), market-mind-portal-build — ⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-08-10: this is NOT the portal deploy, it is a REQUIRED PR TEST context under branch protection. mpl@ derived it and mcl@ verified independently: `grep -ci terraform cloudbuild-portal-build.yaml` = 0, control `cloudbuild.yaml` = 1 so the grep can find terraform; the actual deploy is terraform/07_kubernetes/builds.tf:613 running portal-ui-build.yaml. The exemption protected a TEST as a DEPLOY, and it cost: during the 08-10 closure it was the only trigger left open, so every push spent our highest-volume trigger (92 of 184 builds/day) and bought no required check, because the check it provides was itself disabled. It is GATED as of #8093. The gated set is also where the money is: market-mind-pr-tests $3.00/day, stopbystop-pr-tests $2.91/day and stopbystop-main-tests $2.11/day are three of the four largest line items in the fleet, so gating tests alone reaches the spend without ever blocking a deploy. ensemble-pytest-push and decipher-pytest-push are already disabled upstream and are not ours to re-enable; MarketMindTrigger likewise.
_trigger_region_comment: 2026-08-08 — `regions` and `trigger_region` are DIFFERENT THINGS and conflating them was a real defect caught in the first dry-run. `regions` is where BUILDS LAND and must be swept for costing (market-explorations bills in us-central1 AND global). `trigger_region` is where the TRIGGER OBJECT lives, and there is exactly one. Gating across `regions` tried to disable market-mind-pr-tests in `global`, where no such trigger exists — every hour, forever. It would have failed open so nothing would break, which is precisely why it could have run for weeks as noise nobody read.
